devices.radio: CC1101 sub-GHz ≤20dBm · NFC ST25R3916 · 125kHz RFID in software · IR · iButton · BLE 5.4
devices.is: Pocket multitool for RFID, NFC, sub-GHz and IR.
devices.note: 125kHz RFID runs on MCU comparators with no dedicated chip — the best cost-engineering call in the survey. No Wi-Fi at all. Sub-GHz gap between ~464 and 779MHz.

devices.is: Unreleased Linux successor with swappable SDR modules.
devices.note: Unreleased. The whole market is in wait-and-see until it lands.

devices.radio: Sub-GHz · NFC · 125kHz RFID · IR · Wi-Fi 4 · BLE · 12 GPIO
devices.is: Flipper-style multitool on an STM32H5.
devices.note: Raised 136× its $10k goal in Feb–Mar 2024. Shipped, and widely panned as a brick. Still posting updates two and a half years later.

devices.is: Never delivered.
devices.note: May–June 2025 campaign against a $10,000 goal. A year later: nothing delivered. The single largest failure in the category.

devices.is: Never delivered.
devices.note: Pitched as a GameBoy for hackers in late 2023, shipping promised May 2024. People were publicly calling vaporware by January 2024.

devices.radio: Wi-Fi · BLE · ESP-NOW · NFC/RFID + IR (stretch) · LoRa bundle
devices.is: App-based handheld built around an AMOLED panel.
devices.note: kodeOS turns each sketch into an installable app. A year of design and 50 hand-assembled beta units before launching — which is why it funded.

devices.radio: Wi-Fi · BT · 10/100 Ethernet · CC1101 & LoRa caps optional
devices.is: Pocket Linux computer with a thumb keyboard.
devices.note: 161× its goal. 512MB will bite hard on real Linux workloads. M5Stack had StackChan already in fulfillment — track record is why backers trusted it.

devices.is: Modular Linux handheld with magnetic snap-on parts.
devices.note: 40-pin magnetic snap-on modules, Debian-based Mechanix OS. Revealed at CES 2025, campaign a full year later — that gap is the discipline.

devices.radio: Wi-Fi 6 dual-band ~20dBm · BLE 5.3 · LoRa SX1262 868/915 ~14–20dBm · CC1101 315/433/868/915 · NFC ST25R3916 · 125kHz RFID · IR ×4
devices.is: The most radio-dense multitool made.
devices.note: Six integrated radios — the densest in the survey. GPIO deliberately Flipper-accessory compatible.

devices.radio: Wi-Fi · BLE · IR · nRF24 & CC1101 optional
devices.is: Aluminium-bodied handheld with a Lua app layer.
devices.note: CNC 6061 aluminium unibody with a lanyard loop, Lua app framework, AI chat and MCP control. Firmware fully open.

devices.is: Console-shaped multitool with a games mode.
devices.note: Fully open hardware and firmware, Qwiic/I²C connector. Implementing an Arduboy compatibility layer so existing Arduboy games run unmodified.

devices.radio: Wi-Fi · BLE · ESP-NOW mesh 2–16 units · IR
devices.is: Thumb-sized Wi-Fi and BLE tool driven from a laptop.
devices.note: The smallest goal in the survey and the cleanest delivery. Still the top sub-$50 pick 18 months on. Won on a Rust host CLI streaming into Wireshark, in a 3D-printed case.

devices.is: Dedicated wardriver with no screen — the phone is the UI.
devices.note: Two chips over UART so the scanner is never interrupted. Dual RP-SMA. Direct WiGLE upload, WDG Wars, iOS and Android apps. Sold out; 66 reviews, all five stars. Case STL given away free.

devices.is: Plug-and-play wardriver with GPS on board.
devices.note: Onboard L86-M33 GPS, microSD, pre-flashed Marauder. As of Aug 2026 the only C5 wardriving board with no confirmed defect.

devices.radio: Dual-band Wi-Fi 6 · TI CC1101 sub-GHz · GPS
devices.is: Flipper expansion adding Wi-Fi, sub-GHz and GPS.
devices.note: Flipper Zero expansion board with microSD and USB-C, Marauder preloaded. CNX Software was explicit in March 2026 that the 5GHz wardrive function was unverified and not independently tested. Price drifted from $125 to $140. Listed on Tindie, ships from Czechia.

devices.is: Dev board that became the budget multitool.
devices.note: Cautionary datapoint: the sub-GHz antenna is −0.57dBi and real range tops out near 50m. Same chip everyone else uses. The antenna is the whole story.

devices.is: Receive-only detector. Never transmits.
devices.note: Detection-only, nothing transmitted — which is the entire regulatory strategy. Sky Spy drone RemoteID, Foxhunter RSSI direction-finding, BLE OUI, PCAP, Flock-You camera detection with GPS and KML export.

devices.is: Drone Remote ID detector that alerts over a mesh.
devices.note: FAA Remote ID detection with live web mapping and Meshtastic mesh alerts. Hand-built, about a week out. Covered by CNX Software.

devices.is: Gamma spectrometer that maps radiation as you walk.
devices.note: CsI(Tl) scintillator, 77cps @1µSv/h Cs-137, FWHM 8.4%±0.3%, temp comp −20 to +50°C. Sells on measurement specs, not feature count. GPS-tagged tracks and a shared community spectrum library.

devices.is: Scriptable sub-GHz transceiver for RF research.
devices.note: The most relevant device here. RX amplifier, TX amplifier, and a low-pass filter specifically to kill 800/900MHz harmonics — real front-end engineering. Its weakness is software: reviewers call it unstable and poorly documented.

devices.radio: LoRa/LoRaWAN · Zigbee · Thread · BLE 5.2 · 802.15.4g · 6LoWPAN · Wi-SUN · MIOTY · Matter · Sidewalk · Wireless M-Bus
devices.is: USB stick that sniffs eleven wireless protocols.
devices.note: Closest existing analogue to an RF instrument in this space. Sells through a reseller network — Hacker Warehouse, KSEC, OzHack, PWNLAB — which is how $136 becomes £199 with someone else handling support and VAT.

devices.is: The deepest RFID and NFC research platform.
devices.note: The deepest RFID/NFC research platform. Nothing in the multitool tier comes close on this axis.

devices.is: Keyfob-sized card emulator.
devices.note: Compact RFID/NFC emulation.

devices.is: E-paper writing deck with a tactile keyboard.
devices.note: Solves the screen-versus-runtime tradeoff with two displays. Kit at $210 offloads assembly for only a 19% discount. FCC/CE/UKCA scheduled at the start of the timeline, in parallel with production. Apache-2.0 open hardware.

devices.is: A new board inside a Casio F-91W.
devices.note: A brain transplant for the Casio F-91W. Evidence that a tiny, precisely-scoped product can outperform a broad one.

devices.is: E-paper badge that also emulates RFID.
devices.note: A programmable e-paper badge that emulates RFID. Small, sharp, delivered.

devices.is: Clip-on colour e-paper card for photos and art.
devices.note: The highest funding multiple here by ~300×, and the least technical product. Buyers ask about panel swaps, not specs. Removable panels sold separately turn one hardware sale into recurring revenue.

devices.is: Card-sized sealed Meshtastic tracker.
devices.note: Credit-card size, IP65, magnetic charge cable. 5–10km device-to-device; one vehicle-mounted test hit 100+km. 1,000+ sold at 4.8/5 from 144 ratings.

devices.is: Standalone mesh messenger, no phone needed.
devices.note: Standalone mesh messaging with no phone needed. Base T-Deck is $43–53.

devices.is: Marauder handheld, standalone or bolted to a Flipper.
devices.note: Sold as the M5Shark Manta. Standalone or Flipper Zero GPIO expansion, white or black. 5GHz menus require firmware with C5 dual-band support — several buyer reviews report only 2.4GHz working in practice.

devices.radio: Dual-band Wi-Fi 2.4/5GHz · BLE · GNSS · dual-band antenna
devices.is: Touchscreen Marauder handheld with GNSS.
devices.note: About 80 × 50 × 18mm. Marauder-compatible, USB-C, TF/microSD. Sold explicitly for authorised testing, development and research only — the disclaimer is doing regulatory work, not decoration.

devices.is: Five-radio wardriving board.
devices.note: Marketed as five functions on one board. Batch 1 shipped without WarDrive support at all — the headline feature — and the maker told buyers to wait for Batch 2.

devices.is: Build your own modular phone.
devices.note: Pitched as the first modular DIY phone. $1 reservation locks a 41% discount ahead of the campaign.

devices.is: Build a pair of off-grid encrypted messengers.
devices.note: Ships as a PAIR of encrypted text messengers that work with no SIM card and no cell network. Teaches LoRa, radio frequencies and encryption by building them. The closest thing on the market to a buildable mesh comms kit.

devices.is: Build and code your own smartwatch.
devices.note: Build and code your own smartwatch, then pair it to your phone. Programmed in CircuitBlocks.

devices.is: NASA-branded smartwatch, ready to wear.
devices.note: Officially NASA-themed and ready to use out of the box rather than built — the only non-DIY product in their range. Custom watch faces and apps via CircuitBlocks.

devices.is: Build a handheld games console.
devices.note: Buildable handheld games console. Code your own games in CircuitBlocks.

devices.is: Build and code a virtual pet.
devices.note: Build and code your own handheld virtual pet. No prior knowledge needed.

devices.is: Build a handheld console. Predecessor to ByteBoi.
devices.note: DIY games console, the predecessor to ByteBoi. Sold through Elecrow.

devices.radio: Dual-band Wi-Fi 2.4 + 5GHz · 3× IPEX to PCB-mounted SMA · ATGM336H GPS/GNSS
devices.is: Self-build dual-band wardriver.
devices.note: A revision of Joseph Hewitt's Wardriver with PCB-mounted antennas and the BW16 5GHz mod pre-integrated. Self-assembly kit, case not included — the maker publishes a printable case on Printables instead. Also ships a DS18B20 temperature sensor and SPI microSD. Currently sold out.

devices.is: Specs not published.
devices.note: Their current flagship. Specs not published on the store listing.

devices.raised: Sold in DEF CON drops · US shipping sale TBA
devices.is: Standalone Meshtastic pager that doubles as a LoRa spectrum analyser and packet sniffer.
devices.mcu: ESP32-S3 dual LX7 @240MHz · 512KB SRAM · 2MB PSRAM · 8MB flash
devices.radio: Semtech SX1262 868/915MHz with internal 915 antenna, external supported — LoRa, FSK, GFSK, MSK, GMSK, LR-FHSS · Wi-Fi b/g/n · BLE 5
devices.note: Read and write mesh messages on-device with a custom UI built for the retro LCD. Logs .pcap of Meshtastic, LoRaWAN and other LoRa traffic to a 32GB microSD, decoded in Wireshark with their dissector plugin. Spectrum scan across 850–950MHz with RSSI histogram export. Open source firmware, PCB and 3D-printable mechanicals. 114×84×22.2mm, 191g. 4 directional + 2 action + 1 side button, buzzer, vibration motor, 36 RGB + 12 UV LEDs. Transparent SLA resin body with acrylic panels in clear, fluorescent yellow or orange. Ships fully assembled with belt clip, desk stand and lanyard. Hackaday hands-on July 2025.

devices.is: Compact e-paper Meshtastic handheld with GPS that runs for days.
devices.radio: Semtech SX1262 · US915 / EU868 · L76K GNSS
devices.note: Pre-installed with Meshtastic, flashable to MeshCore. RP-SMA antenna, USB-C. Optional durable enclosure. 93.8% rating on Elecrow's store. Their listing shows $39.90 to $53.90 depending on configuration.

devices.is: Tamagotchi-sized Meshtastic handheld with a bright OLED.
devices.radio: Semtech SX1262 · US915 / EU868 · external antenna
devices.note: Reviewed as one of the smallest ready-to-use Meshtastic handhelds with excellent build quality and a bright screen — but the ESP32-S3 limits it to roughly a day per charge where the nRF52840-based M1 gets 48 hours or more. Battery-less bare board at $18.90 to $21.90.
